title: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disease with Positive Autoimmune Indices: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
case_prompt:
A 45-year-old woman presented with severe mid-thoracic back pain of 1-week duration. On admission, neurologic examination showed impaired sensation to light touch, pain, and vibration in the left lower limb up to the T4 dermatome. MRI of the thoracic spine revealed a T2-hyperintense intramedullary lesion extending from T1 to T7, with contrast enhancement between T1 and T3. Brain MRI and visual evoked potentials were normal.  
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis demonstrated acellularity, normal protein, and negative oligoclonal bands. Serologic testing for HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV, CMV, EBV, HBV, HCV, and HIV in both serum and CSF was unremarkable; PCR for HSV-1 and HSV-2 in CSF was negative. Serum sarcoidosis markers and tumor markers were within normal limits. Immunologic studies showed an ANA titer of 1:320, with negative anti-ENA, anti-dsDNA, anticardiolipin, anti-β2 glycoprotein I antibodies, lupus cells, and cryoglobulins.  
The patient improved after 5 days of intravenous methylprednisolone (1 g daily) followed by an oral corticosteroid taper. Twenty days after completing the taper, she developed chest pain, paraparesis, hyperreflexia, spasticity of both legs, symmetric sensory loss below T4, and urinary retention. Examination revealed bilateral Babinski signs, left lower-extremity strength of MRC grade 1/5, and right strength of grade 2/5. Repeat thoracic MRI showed lesion extension from T1 to T8, and chest CT demonstrated bilateral pleural effusions consistent with serositis.  
Two weeks later, while still on oral corticosteroids, she experienced a second relapse of thoracic myelitis; MRI revealed extension of the lesion to T12. Laboratory tests at that time showed leukopenia, an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and urinary protein excretion of 400 mg over 24 hours.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Infectious causes were considered but excluded — “Testing for antibodies to HSV1, HSV2, VZV, CMV, EBV, HBV, HCV, HIV in serum and cerebrospinal fluid...revealed no pathological values, and PCR in CSF for HSV1 and HSV2 was negative.”  
2. Sarcoidosis and malignancy were considered but ruled out — “sarcoidosis and tumor markers in serum revealed no pathological values. Thoracic and abdominal CT scans were not indicative of any other pathology.”  
3. Multiple sclerosis was considered but made unlikely by the CSF and imaging findings — “Cerebrospinal fluid analysis demonstrated...negative oligoclonal bands,” and the lesion extended over more than three vertebral segments.  
4. Systemic lupus erythematosus was considered given ANA positivity, serositis, mild proteinuria, and elevated ESR — “patient presented several signs of autoimmune disease (positive ANAs, increased sedimentation rate, serositis, mild proteinuria) ...clinical and laboratory findings did not fulfill the diagnostic criteria for SLE.”  
5. Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder was supported by the pattern of recurrent severe myelitis, extensive longitudinal spinal cord lesion, absence of oligoclonal bands, and serologic confirmation — “Taking into account the recurrent severe attacks of myelitis, the extensive spinal cord lesion (Th1–Th12), the absence of oligoclonal bands, the positive autoimmune clinical signs and indices, and the positive NMO-IgG antibodies...it was suggested that the patient was suffering from LETM of the NMO-SD type.”
